{{ElectionsCO}}
The '''2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Colorado''' are to be held on November 8, 2022, to elect the eight [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representatives]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Colorado]], one from each of the state's eight [[Colorado's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections will coincide with the [[2022 Colorado gubernatorial election|Colorado gubernatorial election]], as well as other elections to the [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections|U.S. House of Representatives]], elections to the [[2022 United States Senate elections|U.S. Senate]], and various [[2022 United States elections|state and local elections]].

District boundaries were redrawn to ensure that the districts are [[United States congressional apportionment|apportioned]] based on data from the [[2020 United States census|2020 census]], which added an eighth seat to Colorado's delegation.<ref>{{cite web |title=Colorado's Final Redistricting Congressional Map Could Give Democrats, GOP Equal Number Of Seats |work=CPR News |first=Bente |last=Birkeland |date=September 29, 2021 |url=https://www.cpr.org/2021/09/29/colorado-redistricting-congressional-final-map/}}</ref><ref name="DistrictsFinal">{{cite web |title=Final Approved Congressional Plan |date=September 28, 2021 |work=Colorado Independent Redistricting Commissions |access-date=October 18, 2021 |url=https://coleg.maps.arcgis.com/apps/View/index.html?appid=5b67525550b347219dbfa72482462f3f}}</ref>

{{see also|Colorado's 1st congressional district}}
The 1st district includes almost all of [[Denver]], as well as the enclaves of [[Glendale, Colorado|Glendale]] and [[Holly Hills, Colorado|Holly Hills]].<ref name="DistrictsFinal" /> The district is very similar to its predecessor before 2020 redistricting. The incumbent is Democrat [[Diana DeGette]], who was re-elected with 73.6% of the vote in 2020.<ref name="clerk2020">{{cite web|last=Johnson|first=Cheryl L.|title=Statistics of the Congressional Election of November 3, 2020|url=http://history.house.gov/Institution/Election-Statistics/Election-Statistics/|publisher=[[Clerk of the United States House of Representatives|Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives]]|date=February 28, 2019}}</ref> She is running for re-election.

{{see also|Colorado's 2nd congressional district}}
The 2nd district is located in north-central Colorado, taking in [[Boulder, Colorado|Boulder]], [[Fort Collins, Colorado|Fort Collins]], and [[Longmont, Colorado|Longmont]], as well as the surrounding mountain ski towns, including [[Vail, Colorado|Vail]], [[Grand Lake, Colorado|Grand Lake]] and [[Idaho Springs, Colorado|Idaho Springs]].<ref name="DistrictsFinal" /> The district was made slightly larger during redistricting, and it is now based in the north-central part of the state rather than just west of Denver. The incumbent is Democrat [[Joe Neguse]], who was re-elected with 61.5% of the vote in 2020.<ref name="clerk2020" /> He is running for re-election.
